(out/'REVIEW.md').write_text("The full PR cannot be released. The source-bound ordinary400 packet verifies only targeted feedback for the replacement checkpoint. The native checks reproduce 21 passed, 0 failed and 45 unassessed of 66 approved assertions. A SHA-bound single-reviewer visual evaluation adds two passes and one appearance failure, leaving 23 passed, 1 failed and 42 unassessed. This visual finding is actionable for diagnosis; it has no independent cause consensus and is not a certified product-defect count.

| Case / checkpoint | Evidence and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| ordinary400 ready | 17 unassessed. Top/reveal frames are incidental; the required full-state sweep was deliberately omitted. |
| ordinary400 reviewed | 7 native passes and 9 unassessed. Immediate frame 8 proves the observed action facts and one anchor; it does not cover the remaining planned targets. |
| ordinary400 replaced | 14 native passes; layout and wrapping pass this visual review; action appearance fails this visual review; exact combined surface colors remain unassessed. |
| ordinary400 disabled | 15 unassessed. Original action 4 was never executed. No disabled-tap blocking or callback behavior is claimed. |
| narrow280-large | No native capture in the allowed packet. All 66 required assertions remain unverified for this configuration. |

The independently approved parent plan is unchanged: four checkpoints, 76 matrix cells, 66 required assertions and 10 reasoned N/A cells per fixture. Exact state, action, selector, expectation, unit and source-pointer bindings are retained in [evidence-ledger.json](/Users/rex/Documents/ChatGPT/mobile-native-skill/validation/feedback-forward/neutral-review/pass4/evidence-ledger.json). No original expectation, source file or captured artifact was edited.

The positive provenance checks reconstruct the targeted manifest from the sealed design and original fixture/bridge and match both the fixed request and fresh capture exactly. All neutral source/input seal entries, all 58 portable-file hashes, all explicit native manifest source hashes, original PNG hashes, observation/report receipts, runtime fixture/action values and compiled Bridge bytes match. Current production-source fingerprint equals both captured before/after maps. The source root contains Bridge.swift only; this proves that selected source identity, not a complete compiler dependency graph. No external cache, DerivedData or xcresult path was opened.

The environment API recomputes P for all 22 actual packets: 400 by 600 pt, light, LTR, Dynamic Type large. Native viewport x=1/y=62 and full-app 402 by 874 pt map to the 1206 by 2622 PNGs at scale 3. This is the thin native observer host, not an actual product-page integration pass. The native log independently records ObserverTests.testObserve, exactly one test executed with zero failures. That execution result does not grade the 66 component requirements.

Action 1 retains its original index and target notes.action. Its native dispatch is attempted and succeeds through xcui_tap on one enabled native button. Event interval 0..1 contains exactly notes.reviewed.A, with fixture index 0 and the same PID 10087 / instance FCB3EAD9-CFEB-4519-ADCE-54BA8CB018D3. Action 2 succeeds through caller_fixture_update, advances fixture index 0 to 1 in that same instance, and preserves event interval 1..1 with no callback. The checker passes both callback obligations after these gates; it does not infer quietness from an empty interval alone.

The replacement state is independently bound to input index 1, observation action 3 and stimulus action 2. Frames 12–19 share its input/event/process binding before and after capture. Recomputed native intervals cover 0..2346.333333333333 pt without a gap, with real top and bottom and overlap. Notes title, summary, revision, retained count, button, opening/middle/closing anchors and footer are observed at their exact planned selectors. Button height is 52 pt from native AX geometry; it establishes the approved accessibility-box requirement, not a physical hit region.

I inspected the original PNGs for the entire replacement sweep, plus original frames 7, 8 and 10 around activation and replacement. Their paths and hashes are retained in the visual records. The full sequence visibly preserves all ten cards, the action after card 06 and the end note. Wrapping is readable at this actual environment. Viewport-edge cuts are covered in neighboring frames; they are not treated as content clipping.

The current visual finding is replaced/action-appearance, at notes.action in frames 16 and 17. The approved reference:/visual/disabledAction asks for fill #DCE2E7 and dark text #55616C, rounded corners and at least 52 pt AX height. The rounded action fits and its native height passes, but its fill and label are visibly lighter. A forensic histogram of the entire native action box, mapped through the Skill's image_rectangle API, records dominant fill #EDF0F3 (164795 of 172224 pixels) and common glyph color #A1A8AF (3977 pixels) in each of frames 10, 16 and 17. The original enabled frame 8 instead records dominant #263746 with white glyph pixels. These post-capture whole-box histograms are diagnostic support, not an independently approved pixel sampling policy or computed SwiftUI color evidence. See [diagnostic-action-colors.json](/Users/rex/Documents/ChatGPT/mobile-native-skill/validation/feedback-forward/neutral-review/pass4/diagnostic-action-colors.json) and [visual-observations.json](/Users/rex/Documents/ChatGPT/mobile-native-skill/validation/feedback-forward/neutral-review/pass4/visual-observations.json).

Source diagnosis can start at Bridge.swift lines 45–46 and 110–128: the source palette already declares the intended disabled values, while the runtime disabled action renders differently. Disabled rendering/compositing is a hypothesis to investigate; no specific source cause, minimal patch or retest success has been established. This review makes no claim that every unobserved state has the same appearance problem.

The actual route audit finds no missing route and no unowned assertion against the approved obligation index. With the verified manifest, routing defers 41 unique out-of-scope unassessed assertions to full verification, reviews replaced/neutral-surfaces, and routes the visual failure to diagnose_product. Repeated obligation ownership produces 44 deferred tasks, not 44 independent missing assertions. Without the manifest, the actual tool asks to validate execution scope instead. No missing native capability, failed locator or invalid observed environment has been established by this packet.

Both original automatic-report admission commands, including a request with --scope full, return JSON not_accepted with environment_verified true and source_bound_full_capture false, despite process exit 0. Six MUST obligations block release: current-input, review-state, availability, long-content, readable-layout and appearance. Real-review and quiet-replacement pass their scoped checks. Diagnostic library admission of the legacy visual report also returns not_accepted and records appearance as failed. No admission result certifies the visual judgment.

Next justified work is to preserve this alarm, obtain independent visual/cause review, and resolve exact color evidence under an independently approved policy. The sealed design uses compound string-valued visual clauses and supplies no atomic policy, ownership/sampling configuration, opaque ARGB color atoms, Boolean qualitative atoms or two independent judge submissions. review_contract.catalog actually rejects the missing policy. Therefore the atomic review/acceptance and measured visual-retest path cannot be completed from the allowed artifacts; no new policy or second judge was invented after seeing the pixels.

No source change exists after capture. retest_plan.from_capture actually rejects an unchanged source version, and also rejects a changed source-root namespace. There is no legitimate changed-source retest plan or successful retest to report. If a future authorized diagnosis yields a patch, retain original findings and real before/after source maps, reconstruct the approved review as required, close declared regression dependencies, and then use fresh source-bound feedback. Full final verification must cover all four checkpoints in both fixtures, plus relevant product-page integration checks. The two full manifests were compiled without --run and exactly match the sealed coalesced manifests; [planned-full-ordinary400](/Users/rex/Documents/ChatGPT/mobile-native-skill/validation/feedback-forward/neutral-review/pass4/planned-full-ordinary400/execution.json) and [planned-full-narrow280-large](/Users/rex/Documents/ChatGPT/mobile-native-skill/validation/feedback-forward/neutral-review/pass4/planned-full-narrow280-large/execution.json) are plans only. No further native execution is authorized or was performed.

Actual tool and workflow limitations are retained separately:
- Negative copies with a changed action target, relaxed height expectation or altered PNG are rejected. Wrong-width environment produces F and differs from the fixed approval digest. These marked controls are not product evidence.
- The CLI rejects a newly reviewed report against the original capture's automatic-report byte receipt, with a raw ValueError traceback. Its receipt path accepts the original automatic report; the documented upstream independent acceptance path is unavailable here because its required policy/judges are missing.
- The inner native manifest calls the runtime fixture-file hash execution_coverage.execution_sha256. It differs from the real execution digest. The outer result and independently rebuilt coverage receipt use the correct manifest digest. The inner field is not treated as scope proof.
- The fixed request's opaque tool_snapshot_sha256 lacks a digest definition/file map. Comparing it to one Python file is non-equivalent and cannot establish a snapshot mismatch. All explicitly listed native source hashes do match.
- A local review-input generation command failed with SyntaxError and was corrected before evaluation. Early large tool displays were truncated. The first readout transport envelopes were not all persisted by the review logger; deterministic early readouts were reconstructed from unchanged allowed inputs and labeled as such. Subsequent substantive commands retain full stdout, stderr, argv, times and real child exit codes. These are operator/logging limits, not product defects.

[START.json](/Users/rex/Documents/ChatGPT/mobile-native-skill/validation/feedback-forward/neutral-review/pass4/START.json), END.json and SEAL.json record actual review times and final output hashes. Native timings remain the original producer's nested measurements; no queue duration or isolated agent-compute duration is claimed. No SDK/device command, product edit, expected-input edit, commit, external message, web lookup, other-candidate read or prior-review read was performed.
")
